section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity & Constitution
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The Right to Education became a Fundamental Right through the insertion of Article 21-A. Under which Part of the Constitution does it fall?

options.option_text: Part IV — Directive Principles of State Policy

explanation: Article 21-A sits in Part III (Fundamental Rights). Before the 86th Amendment, free and compulsory education was only a Directive Principle under Article 45 in Part IV.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity & Constitution
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The Fundamental Duty requiring a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child between 6 and 14 years was added by which amendment?
explanation: The 86th Amendment added Article 51-A(k) — the duty of a parent/guardian to provide education opportunities to a child aged 6–14. The original ten duties (Article 51-A(a)–(j)) came via the 42nd Amendment.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity & Constitution
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble of the Constitution by the:
explanation: The 42nd Amendment (the 'Mini-Constitution') inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' into the Preamble.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity & Constitution
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The three-tier Panchayati Raj system and reservation of one-third seats for women were given constitutional status by the:
explanation: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the 11th Schedule for rural local self-government (Panchayats). The 74th Amendment covers urban local bodies (Municipalities). The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age to 18.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity & Constitution
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?

options.option_text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

explanation: Under Article 60, the Chief Justice of India (or, in his absence, the senior-most Supreme Court judge) administers the oath to the President.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity & Constitution
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of:
explanation: DPSP were adopted from the Irish Constitution (which itself drew on Spain). Fundamental Rights echo the USA; parliamentary government the UK; a strong Centre, Canada.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch3 — Indian Polity & Constitution
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The languages recognised by the Constitution of India are listed in which Schedule?
explanation: The Eighth Schedule lists the (currently 22) scheduled languages. The Seventh Schedule holds the Union/State/Concurrent lists; the Sixth covers tribal areas; the Ninth shields certain laws from judicial review.
